scope: Local foundation: packages/core/src/**, packages/store/src/**, packages/store/migrations/**, packages/contracts/src/**, tests/control.test.ts, tests/webhook.test.ts

findings.evidence: packages/core/src/projects.ts:109-116 accepts the same repository/installation/branch binding for multiple projects without an exclusivity check; packages/core/src/github.ts:89-100 uses rows.find, and :108-120 creates a run for only that first project. Configure projects A and B with the same binding, then receive a matching signed push: one explicitly bound project receives no pending-verification run and the globally recorded delivery prevents processing it again for the other project.
findings.refutation: Shared repositories might be intentionally forbidden, or intentionally allowed for monorepos. Neither interpretation makes the existing behavior correct: forbidden duplicates must be rejected during binding; allowed duplicates require explicit routing/fan-out rather than an unordered first match. No uniqueness constraint or duplicate-binding guard exists in the reviewed store schema or migration. The finding concerns local routing and does not assume an external build dispatch.
findings.suggestion: Choose and enforce a binding ownership policy atomically: reject an already-owned repository/installation/branch binding, or support explicit multi-project routing with per-project delivery idempotency. Add a two-project integration case.

remediation_status: Producer acknowledged CORE-001 and is implementing transactional fan-out, a delivery/project uniqueness boundary and an independent regression case. Fix pending; this verdict records the reviewed pre-fix behavior and does not verify remediation.
verified_boundaries: Project-scoped reads check the caller's explicit project IDs; platform lists and mutations require the owner role. Actor authentication itself is outside this library boundary.
Control writes share a database row lock and transaction; intent, idempotency records and audit entries commit atomically on reviewed mutation paths.
GitHub intake checks HMAC over exact raw bytes before parsing; accepted matching pushes remain pending_verification. No branch-head verification or external dispatch is implemented or inferred.
Unconfigured infrastructure operations fail closed without claiming resources were provisioned.
not_reviewed: Production HTTP authentication, identity provisioning and transport authorization: explicitly outside the requested local-foundation scope.
Remote adapters, external dispatch, branch-head verification, hardware isolation, production recovery and infrastructure qualification: not implemented in the reviewed artifact.
PostgreSQL multiprocess execution and failure injection: reasoning review only; caller supplied passing PGlite integration and type-check results, which were not rerun by this critic.
Repository-wide reuse and documentation outside the explicitly assigned paths; reuse and API typing were reviewed only within the scoped artifact.
